## Statement

There are two distinct fixed finite-alphabet multitape interpreters $U_{\rm time}$ and $U_{\rm space}$. On valid $(M,x,\operatorname{bin}(b))$ each reproduces acceptance or rejection reached in at most $b$ simulated transitions, and rejects at expiry; malformed inputs halt rejecting. Put $n=|\langle M,x\rangle|$, including self-delimiting syntax, and let $S$ be the sum of visited simulated cells. For each fixed $M$, the time cost of $U_{\rm time}$ is $O_M(n+b\log(b+2))$ and the visited space of $U_{\rm space}$ is $O_M(n+S+\log(b+2))$, including the decoder and clock. These bounds include $b=0,1$. No fast-time bound is asserted for $U_{\rm space}$, and no linear-$S$ space bound for $U_{\rm time}$.

## Proof status

**Unresolved draft: the time bound is not proved.** The construction below establishes the space part only. It must not be cited as establishing the displayed conjunction. The outstanding obligation is a fixed finite-alphabet geometric-buffer interpreter with a proved redistribution invariant and amortized bound, including a lazy input representation for $b\ll |x|$. The existing Appendix 1.A source checkpoint has not supplied a completed local proof of that obligation.

## Space construction

Extend the tuple syntax of [[def-effective-encoding-of-turing-machines]] by a positive tape count $k$ and by table entries indexed lexicographically by $(q,a_1,\ldots,a_k)$. An entry has one next state, $k$ written symbols and $k$ directions. The header gives $m\ge3$, alphabet size $r\ge1$ and input alphabet size $s<r$; require exactly $(m-2)r^k$ entries, every value in range. Use the same unary-length self-delimiting tuple blocks. This is an extension, not a reinterpretation of existing one-tape codes. Encode $x$ as a tuple of canonical symbol numerals. Input is initialized only on the first simulated tape; the others start blank. All heads start at zero and clamp there, following [[def-turing-machine-initial-and-halting-configuration-interface]] and [[def-multitape-and-nondeterministic-machines]].

Parsing reads a finite word, scans its unary block lengths and rejects missing delimiters, noncanonical numerals, extra bits and out-of-range entries. It counts the actual entries rather than allocating an array of a header-declared size. To compare the expected count with the actual count, multiply with saturation at the actual count plus one. If $r=1$ the power is one; if $r\ge2$, stop after exceeding the actual count. Thus even an enormous malformed tape-count numeral cannot force expansion of an enormous table. On malformed input these finite arithmetic loops terminate and reject. This elaborates the total-decoder argument in [[lem-machine-encoding-is-injective-and-decodable]]; no decoder time bound is used.

For a valid fixed $M$, its tape count, symbol width, state width and table size are constants. On a fixed collection of physical tapes, represent the $k$ virtual tapes by $k$ delimited rows on one tape, each with a single head flag and fixed-width binary symbol records. Include records through the larger of the last initialized nonblank cell and the furthest cell yet visited. Keep the program and encoded input. A sweep over a row locates its flag and reads its symbol into a tuple on a scratch tape. Scanning the fixed program table finds the applicable entry. A second sweep changes the marked symbols and moves each flag to its neighbor, appending a blank record if required. At zero a left flag stays put. Insertion of a record shifts the finite suffix one record to the right, from its right end; it needs only a record-size temporary buffer. Alternatively copying the rows onto another tape uses at most twice their current total length. A state record is updated once all rows have been changed. The unique next configuration is therefore exactly the one specified by [[def-one-step-configuration-relation]], tape by tape. No prior configurations are retained.

If the simulated visited extents are $v_1,\ldots,v_k$, the first row has at most $|x|+v_1+1$ records and every other row at most $v_j+1$. Their total length, with flags and delimiters, is $O_M(n+\sum_j v_j)$. Any scratch copy is bounded by a fixed multiple of this quantity. Store a binary countdown initially equal to $b$, using $O(\log(b+2))$ cells. Before a step, test for halt first, then zero countdown; if neither applies, simulate one transition, decrement, and repeat. Consequently a halt on the $b$th transition is reported, whereas a nonhalting configuration at expiry is rejected. At $b=0$ the nonhalting initial state rejects without simulation; at $b=1$ exactly one transition is permitted. A zero countdown occupies one cell. This proves the claimed space estimate with the resource convention of [[def-machine-time-and-space-constructibility]]. Supplying a constructed clock instead of an input clock adds its separately declared constructor costs.

The physical sweep description may use stationary heads. Store each logical physical-tape symbol at an even cell, leaving the odd cells as spacers. Simulate one logical transition in two physical transitions: a right move uses right-right, a positive-position left move uses left-left, and a stationary action uses right-left. At logical cell zero a clamped left move also uses right-left. Read and write logical symbols only at the even-cell phase; the finite control retains the pending state and directions through the spacer phase. A head flag at logical zero selects the clamped case. Every head therefore returns to a logical symbol boundary simultaneously, and halting is delayed until the second phase. Doubling cell positions and visiting one extra spacer changes space only by a constant factor on the fixed physical tapes. This supplies the allowed left/right-only implementation for the space claim; it is not an amortized-time argument.

## Outstanding time obligation

Neither repeated row scans nor a citation of Appendix 1.A gives $O_M(n+b\log(b+2))$ time. A complete proof still needs an integral-capacity base zone, ordered redistribution, the empty/half/full invariant, charging under intervening higher-level resets, and input initialization costing $O_M(n)$ rather than $O_M(n\log n)$. No local supplier for these statements has been proved here. The source recovery history in the batch coverage remains unchanged. Escalate this exact conjunct to the owner; the separate space argument cannot close it.
